properties.eligibility: Companies and sole proprietors operating in Grindavik (and Svartsengi/HS Orka-linked operations) materially disrupted by the volcanic/seismic emergency since Nov 2023; applications administered via government support measures and municipal/Sudurnes channels; residential property buyout scheme ran separately via Thorkatla (deadline extended to 31 Mar 2025).

properties.type: Sovereign investment/licensing approval regime (Greenland self-government consents under mineral + land/infrastructure competence)
properties.benefits: In April 2026 the Government of Greenland approved transfer of the final 50.5% interest in Tanbreez Mining Greenland A/S to Nasdaq-listed Critical Metals Corp. (CRML), lifting CRML to 92.5% ownership of one of the world's largest undeveloped heavy-rare-earth deposits (all eight defence-critical HREEs; resource re-estimated toward ~130Mt from 45Mt under a March 2026 $30M acceleration program; pilot plant from May 2026, first ore late 2028-early 2029, concentrate export target Q3 2029; US EXIM $120M LOI supports financing); in May 2026 the responsible Ministry approved CRML's acquisition of 70% of 60 North Greenland ApS (construction, logistics, drilling and project-services provider), transferring associated land/asset title - the first foreign-controlled consolidation of in-country mining services capacity; approvals demonstrate Naalakkersuisut's active case-by-case gatekeeping of foreign REE/critical-minerals investment under the 2021 uranium-race repeal framework and its alignment with US/EU/Saudi offtake demand
properties.eligibility: Foreign and domestic mining companies requiring government consent for share transfers, land use and mineral licences in Greenland; Tanbreez precedent sets approval pathway for southern-Greenland REE projects
properties.operator: Naalakkersuisut (Government of Greenland) — Ministry of Industry, Energy, Research & Nature / Ministry responsible for land & infrastructure
properties.status: Both approvals granted (Apr & May 2026); transaction closings in progress
properties.sources: criticalmetalscorp.com + nasdaq.com press releases 17 Apr / 05 May 2026 (company statements of government approvals); investingnews.com + juniorminingnetwork.com + mining.com.au 20 Apr 2026 (independent trade-press confirmation of Naalakkersuisut 50.5% transfer approval); related: ARC-PROG-625 (US EXIM Tanbreez LOI) already in dataset

properties.name: Innovation Norway — Grants for business development in Svalbard (Tilskudd til næringsutvikling på Svalbard)
properties.type: Rolling business-development grant (state aid under GBER)
properties.benefits: Financing and advisory for projects contributing to Svalbard business development; rolling intake via start.innovasjonnorge.no; grant amount depends on project scope; requires responsible business conduct and active sustainability-risk management; distinct from the Research Council of Norway Svalbard Strategic Grant (ARC-PROG-135, research coordination) — this is the commercial næringsutvikling channel
properties.eligibility: Companies with projects contributing to næringsutvikling on Svalbard; must meet five general state-aid (GBER) conditions; no double-funding with SkatteFUNN beyond declared amounts
properties.operator: Innovasjon Norge (Norwegian state enterprise)
properties.status: Open — continuous intake (Norwegian support register updated June 2026)

properties.name: Alaska Power Cost Equalization (PCE) Program — rural electricity rate subsidy
properties.city: Juneau, Alaska (AEA HQ; covers ~193 rural communities statewide)
properties.type: State electricity rate subsidy (endowment-funded)
properties.benefits: Brings rural retail electricity to near-Railbelt-urban levels: state pays the gap between the FY2026 base rate of 20.38 c/kWh and each eligible utility's actual generation cost for the first 750 kWh/month per residence (500 kWh for community facilities); reimburses utilities via AEA on monthly reports; funded by the >US$1B PCE Endowment Fund (AS 42.45.085 allows 5% annual draw, now sufficient for full funding); SB 243 (2022) raised the cap from 500 to 750 kWh; reaches ~82,000 Alaskans in 193 communities; key cost-of-living lever for rural workforce retention and cold-chain/small-industry viability
properties.eligibility: Customers of eligible rural electric utilities determined by the Regulatory Commission of Alaska (RCA); eligibility is community-location based, not income-based; utilities must be RCA-regulated and outside the Railbelt
properties.operator: Alaska Energy Authority (AEA) + Regulatory Commission of Alaska (RCA)
properties.sources: akenergyauthority.org/PCE (official AEA program page: 82,000 customers, 193 communities, AEA+RCA administration, endowment draw) | alaskabeacon.com 16-17 May 2022 (SB 243 signed, 500->750 kWh, 194 communities) | electricchoice.com Aug 2026 (FY2026 base rate 20.38 c/kWh, >$1B endowment)

properties.name: AOGCC Orphan Well Plugging and Remediation Program (IIJA Section 40601)
properties.type: Federal-state remediation grant program (oil & gas legacy cleanup)
properties.benefits: Locates, plugs and restores orphaned oil/gas wells with no legally responsible party on Alaska state and private lands; funded by US DOI grants under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act: USD 25M Initial Grant (Aug 2022; project period Oct 2022-Sep 2025) plus USD 25M Formula Grant Phase 1 (Jun 2024; work period Jul 2024-Jun 2029); plugging service contracts flow to Alaskan small businesses (oilfield services jobs); removes safety and environmental liabilities that block land use and infrastructure siting
properties.eligibility: Wells without a solvent responsible operator on state/private land (state-lead agency role for Alaska under IIJA); Alaska-based contractors and service firms eligible for remediation work contracts; federal wells handled separately by DOI bureaus
properties.operator: Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (AOGCC, DCCED) + US Department of the Interior
properties.status: ACTIVE through Jun 2029 (IIJA orphaned-wells funds obligated through 2030)
properties.sources: commerce.alaska.gov/web/aogcc/OrphanWellsGrant (official AOGCC program page) | scholarworks.alaska.edu UAA-ISER report (2022 initial + 2024 formula grant amounts and periods) | alaskabeacon.com (IIJA funding boost to AOGCC program)

properties.name: Finnmark Estate (FeFo / Finnmarkseiendommen - Finnmárkkuopmodat) common-land industrial lease & value-share regime
properties.type: Community-owned land & resource institution (industrial ground-lease regime + redistribution grants)
properties.benefits: FeFo owns and manages ~95% of the land and surface water in Finnmark (formerly state land, transferred 1 Jul 2006 under the Finnmark Act) on behalf of all residents - Norway's second-largest landowner; grants land/water leases and fallrett (waterfall rights) rents for industrial use; holds priority wind/hydro development rights via Finnmark Kraft AS (FeFo + 7 local energy companies; 15-year pre-emption on new builds on FeFo ground; co-owns Hamnefjell and Havoygavelen wind parks with institutional capital); redistributes ~10% of turnover to local projects (NOK 6.3M in 2023 via Giisa grants); residents (bosatte) get priority access to hunting/fishing/tourism quotas - the de-facto gatekeeper for Arctic energy, tourism and mining surface access in Finnmark
properties.eligibility: Industrial leases/permits open to companies operating in Finnmark with local-resident priority; Giisa project grants to Finnmark-based associations and projects; board = 3 members appointed by Finnmark County Council + 3 by the Sameting (Sami Parliament)
properties.operator: Finnmarkseiendommen - Finnmárkkuopmodat (FeFo), self-governing institution under Lov om forvaltning av land og naturressurser i Finnmark (Finnmarksloven) 17 Jun 2005
properties.sources: fefo.no/om-fefo + fefo.no/naring/fornybar-energi (official: 95% of Finnmark land, Finnmark Kraft AS pre-emption, fallrett rents) | sciencedirect.com Land Use Policy (2019) FeFo land-tenure reform study | thenorthernreview.ca issue 39 (2015) 'The Finnmark Estate' institutional analysis

properties.name: Greenland Exploitation-Licence Reform - early-granting regime under the amended Mineral Resources Act (3 licences in 2025: GAM anorthosite, Isua iron, Amitsoq graphite)
properties.city: Nuuk (Mineral Resources Authority / Naalakkersuisut, Department of Business and Mineral Resources)
properties.type: Regulatory fast-track regime (early granting of 30-year exploitation licences)
properties.benefits: Amendment to the 2009 Mineral Resources Act allows the Government of Greenland to grant the political Exploitation Licence EARLY - after Terms of Reference + White Paper approval and before final EIA/SIA reports - compressing time-to-permit (Amitsoq graphite: licence 1 yr 3 mo after application vs typical 18-36 months of additional review); three 30-year exploitation licences issued in 2025 (GAM anorthosite 21 May; third = Greenland Graphite Amitsoq 8 Dec), signalling a deliberate policy push to attract responsible Arctic critical-minerals investment while retaining environmental, safety and social standards + mandatory Impact Benefit Agreements with municipalities; for trade-lane intelligence: converts Greenland from exploration-only to a permitting jurisdiction with defined construction/production deadlines (mine plan by 31 Dec 2028, production start by 31 Dec 2030 for Amitsoq)
properties.eligibility: Any licensed mineral project holder applying under the amended Act; political approval of ToR/White Paper precedes licence; EIA/SIA + public consultation + Impact Benefit Agreement remain binding conditions before mine construction
properties.operator: Naalakkersuisut - Government of Greenland, Minister for Business, Mineral Resources, Energy, Justice and Gender Equality (Naaja H. Nathanielsen); Mineral Resources Authority (MRA)
properties.status: ACTIVE since 2024 amendment (applied across 2025 licence grants)
properties.sources: govmin.gl licence announcements 21 May 2025 + 8 Dec 2025 (official, 'recent legal amendment that allows for early granting of exploitation licences') | kalkine.co.uk GreenRoc note ('revised Mining Act... streamline approvals') | mining.com 9 Dec 2025 | minexforum.com 11 Dec 2025

properties.name: NRC IRAP — Clean Technology Stream (cleantech R&D funding, SDTC-mandate absorption)
properties.type: Federal R&D grant (clean-technology stream of NRC-IRAP)
properties.benefits: Non-repayable contributions + Industrial Technology Advisor (ITA) support for SMEs commercializing clean technologies; absorbed the Sustainable Development Technology Canada (SDTC) programming mandate following the 4 Jun 2024 transfer; TRL 5-6 project gating with measurable environmental-benefit requirements; typical awards CAD 100K-500K; stackable with SR&ED tax credits; part of IRAP's four-stream architecture (Core / Clean Technology / Defence Industry Assist / AI-adjacent) that paid CAD 393.1M to 3,136 SMEs in FY2024-25
properties.eligibility: Incorporated for-profit Canadian SME (<=500 FTE) developing innovative clean-tech products/processes/services with quantifiable environmental benefit; must engage an NRC ITA
properties.operator: National Research Council Canada (NRC IRAP) — Clean Technology stream
properties.sources: nrc.canada.ca 'Support for technology innovation' (OFFICIAL NRC page; clean-technology support listing); grantcompass.ca IRAP 2026 guide (4 Jun 2024 Minister of ISI announcement SDTC->NRC transfer, TRL 5-6 gating, $100K-500K awards, FY24-25 $393.1M/3,136 SMEs per NRC 2024-25 Departmental Results Report); hellodarwin.com NRC funding programs 2026 (official program listing 'NRC IRAP - Support for clean technology'). properties.name: Canada Innovation Corporation (CIC) — federal Crown-corp consolidation of innovation funding (designated NRC-IRAP successor)
properties.type: Institutional regime (Crown corporation transition)
properties.benefits: Announced 19 Dec 2023: full implementation of the Canada Innovation Corporation no later than 2026-27, consolidating fragmented federal innovation funding (with NRC-IRAP as centrepiece) into a single mission-driven Crown corporation under the Canada Development Investment Corporation (CDIC) portfolio; IRAP remains at NRC until transition with ITA-led model and active files carried forward; materially affects how northern/territorial SMEs (Yukon/NWT/Nunavut IRAP service points, ARC-PROG-164) apply for federal R&D funding

properties.name: Nordic Council of Ministers — Ministerial Declaration on Zero-Emission Shipping Routes (Green Corridors) between Nordic countries + Nordic Roadmap: Future Fuels for Shipping pilot
properties.city: Oslo (declaration adopted, May 2022; NCM secretariat Copenhagen)
properties.type: Regional intergovernmental regime (green shipping corridor demand signal + pilot funding)
properties.benefits: Nordic climate and environment ministers agreed (May 2022, under the Oslo Declaration) to work jointly to establish green corridors for emission-free shipping between ports in the Nordic Region, building on the post-COP26 commitment to six emission-free corridors; follow-up pilot 'Nordic Roadmap for the Introduction of Sustainable Zero-Carbon Fuels in Shipping' (funded by the Nordic Council of Ministers, running to 2027, led by DNV with IVL Swedish Environmental Research Institute, SINTEF Ocean, VTT, Everllence and Icelandic New Energy) maps intra-Nordic green corridor candidates (report 16 May 2023), creates coordinated demand and investment pull for zero-emission fuels, ships, bunkering and port infrastructure, and aligns Nordic positions for EU (FuelEU Maritime) and IMO negotiations (incl. 'polar fuel' proposals); for trade-lane intelligence: defines which Nordic Arctic-adjacent routes (Norwegian Sea, North Atlantic between Greenland/Faroe/Iceland/Norway) are being engineered toward zero-emission operation by ~2030
properties.eligibility: Pilot project participation open to Nordic maritime stakeholders (ports, shipowners, fuel suppliers, classification societies, research institutes) via the NCM-funded roadmap project; corridor realisation depends on national co-funding (e.g. Enova-backed vessel concepts like the ammonia-powered Yara Eyde in the Oslofjord corridor launched Feb 2026)
properties.operator: Nordic Council of Ministers (norden.org) — Ministers for Climate and Environment; pilot led by DNV (Norway)
properties.status: ACTIVE (declaration May 2022; roadmap pilot funded to 2027; first Nordic zero-emission freight corridor service launched Feb 2026)
properties.sources: norden.org ministerial declaration page + norden.org/en/news 'Clear to proceed - green shipping corridors in the Nordic region' (OFFICIAL NCM) | ivl.se press release 2025-12-19 (Nordic Roadmap funded by NCM to 2027, DNV-led consortium incl. IVL/SINTEF/VTT/Everllence/Icelandic New Energy) | futurefuelsnordic.com 'Intra-Nordic green shipping corridor candidates' PDF 16 May 2023 (NCM pilot deliverable) | pub.norden.org politiknord2022-724 (six emission-free corridors commitment post-COP26) | bunkermarket.com 5 Feb 2026 (NCL/Yara Oslofjord zero-emission corridor launch, Enova funding). properties.name: Nordkalottrådet (Nordkalott Council / Pohjoiskalotin neuvosto) Cross-Border Project Grant Scheme — Nordic Border Region Co-financing
properties.city: Luleå, Sweden (joint office at Region Norrbotten, Robertsviksgatan 7)
properties.type: Cross-border regional co-financing grants (intergovernmental Nordic political council, Nordic Council of Ministers-backed)
properties.benefits: Small cross-border project grants typically EUR 1,000-10,000 covering up to 50% of project budget; a single activity may be co-financed at most two consecutive years, after which other funding sources must be secured; award criteria = partners drawn from ALL member regions + demonstrable Nordic added value + novelty (not previously done in the same way) + alignment with the adopted 2025-2027 action programme (green Norden / competitive Norden / socially sustainable Norden); the Council also runs Gränstjänsten Sverige-Finland-Norge (free cross-border labour/legal/tax barrier advisory, offices in Storfjord NO and Tornio FI) and Nordkalottens Miljöråd (joint nature-protection/environmental sub-council); founded 1967 as Nordkalottkommittén, renamed Nordkalottrådet 1997; 12 political members (4 each from NO/SE/FI), meetings 1-3x/year, chair rotates every three years between Norwegian counties, Lapland and Region Norrbotten; co-financed by the Nordic Council of Ministers regional-development programme. For trade-lane intelligence: this is the cheapest entry ticket for Arctic border-region SME/trailblazer cooperation (ports, tourism, competence, transport connectivity on the Nordkalotten) that sits BELOW Interreg thresholds and does not require ERDF-level project machinery.
properties.eligibility: Registered public/private actors and civil-society organisations located in the Nordkalott border regions — Norway (Nordland, Troms, Trøndelag counties), Sweden (Norrbotten, Västerbotten), Finland (Lapland, North/Central Ostrobothnia) — able to form a partnership with counterparts from all three member countries; applications assessed by the Council's office (Region Norrbotten).
properties.operator: Nordkalottrådet / Pohjoiskalotin neuvosto (secretariat hosted by Region Norrbotten)
properties.status: Active — 2025-2027 action programme adopted at the spring meeting in Bodø
properties.sources: https://nordkalottradet.org/hae-tukea-sv/ (OFFICIAL council grant rules: EUR 1,000-10,000, max 50%, partners from all member countries, max 2 consecutive co-financings, Region Norrbotten contact) | https://nordkalottradet.org/neuvoston-esittely-sv/ (OFFICIAL council profile: founded 1967, renamed 1997, 12 members, Gränstjänsten offices Storfjord/Torneå, Miljöråd sub-council, NCM co-financing) | https://www.regeringen.se/contentassets/250aaab422dc49c5a1c94225647bf093/nordkalottradet.pdf (OFFICIAL Swedish Government — Nordkalottrådet statement on the EU MFF 2028-2034, Interreg as core border-region financing platform) | https://nordkalottradet.org/uutinen/nordkalottradets-prioriteringar-under-kommande-tre-aren/ (2025-2027 priorities, Bodø spring meeting)

properties.name: Uppbyggingarsjóður Vestfjarða (Westfjords Development Fund) — Sóknaráætlun Vestfjarða 2025-2029 competitive grants
properties.type: Competitive regional development grant fund (business development, innovation and culture)
properties.benefits: Approx. ISK 50M distributed per annual round (2026 window: ~ISK 50M available after ISK 15M already earmarked for multi-year grants); grants capped at 50% of eligible project costs; three categories — (1) employment/business development & innovation, (2) culture, (3) endowment and operating support for year-round cultural institutions; 2026 allocation announced: ISK 7.0M in core/operating grants plus ISK 19.35M to 24 business-development & innovation projects, from 133 applications with 67 funded (50.4% success rate); 2023 baseline for comparison: 103 applications, 62 funded, ISK 43.3M new + ISK 11.85M multi-year carry-over = ISK 55.15M across 69 projects; decisions by a five-member úthlutunarnefnd elected at the Fjórðungsþing (quarter-assembly) with north-Westfjords / south-Westfjords / Strandir / Reykhólar representation plus two external members, advised by two fagráð panels (culture; business development & innovation); applications submitted through the Rannís (Icelandic R&D and innovation agency) grant gateway, which now offers an English interface; autumn deadline (noon, 22 October for the 2026 round). For trade-lane intelligence: this is the only grant instrument dedicated to the Vestfirðir district (~7,168 residents, depopulating) whose port/town economy is cruise, fisheries and energy-transition driven — it co-firms the Ísafjörður node as a funded entrepreneurship territory rather than a purely touristic one.
properties.eligibility: Legal-age individuals, community groups, companies and institutions based in the Vestfirðir region holding an Icelandic identification number (kennitala); projects must serve the Westfjords and align with Sóknaráætlun Vestfjarða 2025-2029; core/operating grants restricted to cultural institutions operating on a full-year basis.
properties.operator: Vestfjarðastofa (Westfjords Regional Development Office, self-governing entity founded 1 Dec 2017) on behalf of Fjórðungssamband Vestfirðinga
properties.status: Active — annual autumn allocation round; 2026 grants awarded

properties.name: BOCOD — Boosting Continuity and Digitalisation of Rural Region Businesses (Interreg NPA 2025-2028; Westfjords + East Iceland rural SME succession/digital programme)
properties.country: Iceland / Finland / Ireland (transnational; Icelandic delivery in Vestfirðir & Austfirðir)
properties.city: Ísafjörður (Vestfjarðastofa partner office); lead partner Cork, Ireland
properties.type: EU/EEA Interreg Northern Periphery & Arctic transnational cooperation project (free technical assistance + training for rural SMEs)
properties.benefits: Total project budget EUR 1.499M of which EUR 974,736.04 is NPA (ERDF + EEA/Norwegian) programme funding; Vestfjarðastofa's own share EUR 100,000; delivers at no cost to rural micro/small enterprises: mapped inventory of existing support schemes (100+ national/regional/EU instruments analysed for gaps), a living roadmap for digitalisation and business continuity, digital-skills training and mentoring, and pilot mechanisms for business transfer/succession planning so firms are bought and continued rather than closed; three work packages — WP1 resource mapping (MTU Hincks Centre, IE), WP2 targeted digital training (Lapland University of Applied Sciences, FI), WP3 business-continuity/transfer pilots (Business Joensuu Ltd, FI); first transnational meeting 26-28 Aug 2025 at University of Oulu (Kerttu Saalasti Institute / MicroENTRE) with stakeholder input, surveys, focus groups and interviews feeding the 2025-2026 outputs; builds on the earlier Interreg NPA 'Eboost' project. For trade-lane intelligence: successor shortage is the binding constraint on Arctic coastal/port service businesses (fish processing, harbour logistics, guiding, retail) — BOCOD is the instrument that keeps those nodes operating rather than transferring ownership out of the region.
properties.eligibility: Rural and sparsely-populated-area micro and small enterprises (plus the organisations that support them) in the programme's Icelandic regions (Vestfirðir via Vestfjarðastofa, Austfirðir via Austurbrú), Finnish North Karelia/Ostrobothnia/Lapland and Irish Munster; participation is via the regional development offices' training and transfer-support activities rather than a competitive grant call.

properties.name: Greenland Uranium Act (Act No. 20 of 1 Dec 2021) — ban on uranium investigation/exploration/exploitation + 100 ppm by-product ceiling (zero-tolerance reinstated)
properties.type: Mining-sector legislative regime (investment gate)
properties.benefits: Prohibits preliminary investigation, exploration and exploitation of uranium AND any non-uranium mineral project whose average uranium content of the total resource exceeds 100 ppm by weight (Sec.1); government may extend the ceiling to other radioactive elements; violations punishable by fines, corporate criminal liability under Ch.5 of the Greenland Criminal Code; government may restrict/revoke existing mineral licences; direct legal basis for Naalakkersuisut's 9 Jun 2023 formal rejection of the Kuannersuit/Kvanefjeld REE+U exploitation licence (ETM/Greenland Minerals) and the company's ongoing DKK 15B (~USD 2.2B / A$3.3B) compensation arbitration in Denmark; shapes all rare-earth investment screening in Greenland since Dec 2021. LITIGATION MILESTONE 01-Sep-2026: High Court of Greenland ruled predominantly in favour of subsidiary Greenland Minerals A/S on which Greenlandic defendants remain parties to the Kvanefjeld proceedings — all defendants stay in except Inatsisartut (Parliament, defendant 7) and the Self-Government (defendant 8), with the court holding (per established Danish practice) that challenges to the lawfulness of enacted legislation and related damages claims must be directed against the executive branch, so Naalakkersuisut (Government of Greenland) remains a defendant; merits phase cleared: defendant responses on the merits due 27-Oct-2026, parties to advise anticipated oral-hearing duration by 10-Nov-2026, hearing could be scheduled as early as autumn 2027 or H1-2028; parallel Danish litigation against the Danish Government unaffected, remains pending but paused
properties.eligibility: All mineral-rights applicants and licence-holders in Greenland; uranium-bearing REE deposits (Kvanefjeld, Kringa, Motzfeldt Centre) effectively excluded from exploitation licensing while Act is in force

properties.name: MTOR — International Territory for Advanced Socio-Economic Development (Международная территория опережающего развития) — new foreign-investor preferential regime, RF effective 1-Jan-2026
properties.country: Russia (Far East FD: Amur Oblast, Jewish AO, Primorsky Krai, Zabaykalsky Krai, Khabarovsk Krai)
properties.city: Vladivostok (Primorsky Krai — site of first planned MTOR under RF-PRC intergovernmental agreement)
properties.type: Preferential investment regime (new TOR chapter, Federal Law 285-FZ)
properties.benefits: Newest Russian preferential regime layered on the TOR system: MTOR is a discrete land plot (max 20 km2, ~10-20 industrial complexes) inside a Far East FD municipality with a special legal regime for high-value-added manufacturing with foreign participation. Resident benefits: 0% federal profit-tax rate for 10 years (regional part reducible to 0% by subject law for 10 yrs); reduced insurance contributions 7.6% (for capex >= RUB 500M); free customs zone (СТЗ) procedure; land plot + infrastructure connection from management company; single-window administration + limited inspections; up to 100% compensation of CBR refinancing rate on infrastructure construction loans; tax stability guarantees for 15 years from registry entry (no worsening of conditions); special approval track for projects >= RUB 10B; foreign banks may open an additional branch on MTOR territory; public access to resident beneficiary/management info can be closed (sanctions protection). Created either by Government decision or by an international treaty of the RF — the treaty track is what makes it 'international'.; site pipeline detail (Chekunov via Interfax/Vedomosti 21-Jul-2025): total MTOR investment pipeline ~RUB 20B, shortlist ~10 projects; Amur Oblast MTOR site = platform "Rovnoye" (Ровное), target >=RUB 10B in first 3 years; remaining first-wave sites in EAO, Zabaykalsky, Khabarovsk and Primorye krais; eastrussia.ru: RUB 5.5B into Amur MTOR infrastructure — SUPERSEDED by official figure: >RUB 6B regional budget for Rovnoye greenfield infra (KRDV erdc.ru + ampravda.ru 29-Aug-2025); see dedicated site row ARC-PROG-708 (MTOR Rovnoye profile, 25B portfolio / 10B MTOR share / anchors WB+Ozon+BAGK+Xuanyuan)
properties.eligibility: New Russian legal entity (foreign founders/entities permitted) registered on the MTOR, concluding an activity agreement and entered in the MTOR residents registry; minimum capital investment RUB 500M; must produce high-value-added goods (per-government list); individual entrepreneurs excluded; from 2026 residents may also perform government-listed works/services
properties.operator: Minvostokrazvitiya RF (policy) / AO KRDV-ERDC (management & registry); created by Federal Law of 31.07.2025 No. 285-FZ amending 473-FZ (chapter on MTOR) + tax law Federal Law of 22.07.2025 amending NK RF arts. 5/284/427; regime operative from 1-Jan-2026
properties.status: ACTIVE (regime in force since 01-Jan-2026; first MTOR planned via RF-PRC intergovernmental agreement in Primorsky Krai — draft transmitted to Chinese side Oct-2025 per Minvostokrazvitiya)

properties.name: Norwegian Security Act screening of Kirkenes Havn — government freeze on Chinese port presence (sikkerhetsloven kartlegging, Longyearbyen next)
properties.type: National-security regulatory regime (governance row affecting port development & foreign investment)
properties.benefits: Regime row for the state's override of Kirkenes port's China pivot: after NRK exposés of Kirkenes Havn KF harbour chief Terje Jørgensen's contacts with CCP-controlled COSCO (incl. Helsinki meeting 2024 and intermediaries Yingxiang Zhao/HNDG network), the Government in Sep-2024 formally blocked Chinese establishment at Kirkenes: Minister of Justice and Public Preparedness Emilie Enger Mehl (Sp) — 'national security comes first', government prepared to say no to Chinese actors; Nærings- og fiskeridepartementet sent a letter to the port invoking the Security Act (sikkerhetsloven) and launched a mapping of whether parts of the port area are of national security significance (same instrument used to stop the 2021 Bergen Engines-TMH sale). In Sep-2025 fisheries/ocean policy minister Marianne Sivertsen Næss confirmed to NRK the mapping is intensified given the security-political situation, with Longyearbyen havn (Svalbard) announced as the next port to be screened; PST annual threat assessment singles out Chinese business actors seeking strategic infrastructure footholds in the North; NSD rates northern ports as intelligence targets. Port maintains investment/sale to Chinese companies was never contemplated; municipal friction (mayor Magnus Mæland: dialogue with PST; Øst-Finnmark growth vs security trade-off). Practical effect: any Kirkenes transshipment-hub or NSR-linkage scenario requiring Chinese capital/operators is frozen pending kartlegging outcome; complements ARC-PROG-257 (Kirkenes Havn KF dissolution into Sør-Varanger kommune from 2027 + Stamnett terminal planning) which is the ownership-restructuring row.
properties.eligibility: Applies to Kirkenes Havn KF assets/leases/access; screening under sikkerhetsloven by Nærings- og fiskeridepartementet with Justis- og beredskapsdepartementet; potential follow-on protection designation; Longyearbyen havn next in queue
properties.operator: Kingdom of Norway (Nærings- og fiskeridepartementet + Justis- og beredskapsdepartementet); executed via Security Act powers
properties.status: ACTIVE (kartlegging ongoing since Sep-2024; intensified Sep-2025; Longyearbyen screening announced; no public conclusion as of Sep-2026)
properties.sources: nrk.no 'Vil kartlegge havnenes betydning for nasjonal sikkerhet' (minister Næss quote, Sep-2024 sikkerhetsloven use, Longyearbyen next) + bt.no 'Regjeringen vil ikke åpne for kinesiske etableringer i Kirkenes havn' (JD press release, Mehl quotes) + dagsavisen.no same JD statement + anlegg.bygg.no (NFD letter to port invoking sikkerhetsloven, Cosco dialogues) + nrk.no investigation series (havnesjefen-Cosco Helsinki 2024; 'Kinas polare silkevei' longform; motstridende råd) + kirkeneshavn.no OFFICIAL-PORT (project pages, port statements) + kids.kiddle/kids data: cruise lines dropped Kirkenes 2022 over Russian-border proximity (context), conf 88, VERIFIED, name-disambig from ARC-PROG-010 (frozen deep-water port + Arctic Railway row, pre-2022 COSCO courting) and ARC-PROG-257 (KF dissolution/integration 2027) — this is the 2024-2026 Security Act governance/screening row

properties.name: Isaaffik Arctic Gateway — Kingdom of Denmark polar research coordination & logistics-sharing platform (Nuuk–Copenhagen–Aarhus knowledge corridor)
properties.type: Research-infrastructure coordination platform (institutional row)
properties.benefits: Platform row: 'Isaaffik' is Greenlandic for 'gateway' — a user-driven web platform (isaaffik.org) supporting Arctic research and collaboration among universities and knowledge centres within the Kingdom of Denmark, run under the Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science (Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen, ufsn.dk) polar research collaborations programme. Users advertise expeditions, fieldworks, events, courses/education, infrastructure and logistics; search by list/map/timeline; expedition-matching to share costs; covers legislation for research/expeditions in Greenland (Joint Arctic Command permissions). Partner institutions: Aarhus University, Aalborg University, Asiaq Greenland Survey, Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI), Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science, GEUS (Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland), Greenland Institute of Natural Resources, the Greenlandic Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Church (Naalakkersuisut), Joint Arctic Command, National Museum of Denmark, DTU, University of Copenhagen, University of Greenland (Ilisimatusarfik), University of Southern Denmark. Listed in RoPON (Polar Observing Platforms Network) registry Mar-2026. Pipeline coupling: Grønlands Forskningsråd/NALU grant recipients (ARC-PROG-695) must publish projects on Isaaffik — this is the infrastructure/visibility layer of the Kingdom's Arctic research-funding stack, relevant to any research-station, sampling or logistics project in the GIS atlas.
properties.eligibility: Open sign-up for anyone engaged in Arctic research, education, infrastructure and logistics (institutions + individuals within and beyond the Kingdom); content posting subject to platform rules; Greenland fieldwork requires government/JAC permission workflows documented on-platform
properties.operator: Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen (Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science) with Kingdom research institutions; platform operated as user-driven collaboration
properties.sources: ufsn.dk (Ministry of Higher Education & Science, OFFICIAL-DK-GOV: full partner list incl. properties.name: TOR 'Chukotka' (ASEZ) 2025-26 resident-pool expansion — 18 new residents RUB 12.3B mining portfolio + Decree-1803 boundary extension for Baimskaya GOK
properties.type: Advance socio-economic development zone (ASEZ/ТОР) preferential regime — resident-pool expansion row
properties.benefits: Regime+pipeline row for Russia's Arctic-facing mining ASEZ: in 2025 eighteen companies received ТОР 'Chukotka' resident status with a combined RUB 12.3B investment plan (announced by the Chukotka AO government press service, 20-Jan-2026) — key new projects: Polymetall's backfill (закладочный) complex with infrastructure at the Mayskoye gold deposit (157 km from Pevek, one of Russia's largest gold objects), plus two Svarog LLC projects combining precious-metal extraction with hazardous-waste/tailings reprocessing (gold+palladium recovery). Coincides with RF Government Decree No. 1803 of 14-Nov-2025 extending ТОР 'Chukotka' boundaries by >20,000 ha in Pevek municipal district and Bilibino district to unlock the Baimskaya copper-molybdenum GOK (46 production/infrastructure objects incl. a year-round port terminal and a 400+ km all-weather road to the Arctic coast; PSB bank financing >RUB 100B confirmed 2026; startup targeted 2030, ~2 Mt/yr concentrate via NSR). Standing regime benefits per ERDC (management company KRDV Chukotka): insurance contributions cut to 7.6% for 10 years, reduced profit/property/land taxes, free customs zone procedure, land provision + infrastructure support, legal protection; 48 permitted activity types, mining dominant. Portfolio scale per ERDC/KRDV 10-year TOR anniversary (Aug-2026): 55 residents implementing 55 investment projects worth >RUB 1 trillion, >9,700 jobs planned; anchor resident Beringpromugol (Fandyushkinskoye coal); total regional resident base (ТОР+СПВ+АЗРФ) 93 companies / RUB 873B+ announced. Complements ARC-PROG-696 MTOR (new international regime) and ARC-PROG-001 AZRF 193-FZ tax regime (all-Chukotka overlay) — this is the ТОР instrument's 2025-26 mining-pipeline row. VEB.RF session at VEF-2026 (3-Sep-2026): GDK Baimskaya investment plan revised up to >RUB 731B (vs RUB 360B signed at VEF-2019), Chukotka GRP +55% projected on construction, consolidated district budget revenues RUB 8B over 2028-2033.
properties.eligibility: Legal entities/IE registered within ТОР boundaries (Anadyr, parts of Anadyr and Bilibino districts, Pevek-area extension) with min RUB 500k investment, no branches outside ТОР, activity on the 48-item permitted list; new-land parcels in Pevek MO/Bilibino for Baimskaya-linked projects under Decree 1803

properties.name: ETOR 'Unified Territory of Advanced Development' (Единая ТОР) — RF bill to merge all Far East & Arctic preferential regimes from 2027

properties.type: Preferential regime (planned federal law, regime consolidation); APR-2026 CONCEPT REVISION (nedradv.ru 20-Apr-2026): Minvostokrazvitiya lowered entry threshold from RUB 10M to RUB 5M, tied tax preferences to project profitability, proposed 50% levy on "super-profit" of ETOR residents (70% regional / 30% federal budget; RSPU lobbying revision; Minfin proposes expanding permitted activities); umbrella change already enacted for current regimes via Federal Law 18-FZ of 11-Feb-2026 (new Art. 56.1 NK RF: tax savings capped at actual capex, TVmax TOR mechanism, regions align laws by 1-Dec-2027; covered in ARC-PROG-199/427); VEF-2026 PLENARY 3-Sep-2026: President Putin declared the unified regime operates across the ENTIRE Far East + Arctic from 1-Jan-2027 with a "menu of benefits" (reduced insurance contributions, tax + customs preferences, infrastructure hook-up support) NOT tied to any specific special zone or TOR; Chekunov 2-Sep-2026: bill to State Duma autumn session 2026, oil & gas extraction + financial + excise activities EXCLUDED from benefits, ETOR territory >50% of Russia, parameters reconciled with Minfin and all 19 DFO/Arctic regions; existing TOR/SPV residents keep current benefits in full
properties.benefits: Presidential directive to create a single unified preferential regime (ETOR) merging and harmonizing ALL existing macro-regional regimes of the Far Eastern Federal District and the Arctic Zone (TOR/ASEZ, Free Port of Vladivostok, KORF Kuril Islands, SAR Special Administrative Districts, AZRF 193-FZ, and the new MTOR international regime per Chekunov's MTOR list); concept work took ~1 year; bill to be submitted to the State Duma as soon as the new convocation is formed, with entry into force targeted 1-Jan-2027; announced by Minvostokrazvitiya chief Aleksey Chekunov at the Sep-2-2026 meeting on DFO development in Vladivostok (VEF-2026 week); ministry will report to President Putin on ETOR launch in Arctic and Far East; rationale: single rulebook for investors replacing 6+ overlapping regimes with different tax/customs/insurance benefit stacks; existing resident contracts expected to migrate into unified framework; VEF-2026 follow-up (2-3 Sep 2026): only NEW investment projects will receive ETOR support (murmantv.ru); fiscal case cited by Chekunov — regime residents generated RUB 723B of taxes vs RUB 373B of benefits over 10 years, two design principles: non-deterioration of existing benefits + calibration with Minfin (konkurent.ru/primpress.ru); law to be adopted during autumn session of new Duma by end-2026 for 1-Jan-2027 entry (kommersant.ru) | VEF-2026 PARAMETER REVEAL (3 Sep 2026, Putin plenary + Chekunov meeting): insurance premiums for ETOR residents cut to 15%; TWO resident categories by investment volume — RUB 100M-1B gets the basic benefits menu, RUB 1B+ chooses between the full TOR-analog package OR the federal investment tax deduction; simplified construction permitting incl. waived state expertise of design docs; land plots provided WITHOUT auctions; regime created by merging TOR + Free Port of Vladivostok tools; 10-year track record cited: residents paid RUB 723B taxes vs RUB 373B preferences = net RUB 350B budget profit; bill drafted with all 19 DFO/Arctic regions + State Duma + Federation Council + business; to be filed with the NEW State Duma convocation, effective 1-Jan-2027

properties.name: Kraftlyftet — Swedish Energy Agency national power-system investment support (production & storage + energy efficiency tracks)
properties.city: Eskilstuna (Swedish Energy Agency HQ; nationwide, northern Sweden industrial-expansion driven)
properties.type: State investment support (investeringsstöd) under two EU-approved Swedish aid regulations
properties.benefits: Track 1 "Produktion och lagring": grants for investments securing electricity-system delivery reliability or enabling grid connection of new electricity demand — bio-CHP conversions, new gas turbines, energy storage, upgraded output of existing plants; regulation adopted by government Dec-2025; first call 26-Feb to 07-May-2026 (application window closed 01-Jul-2026 per agency page), utlysta medel SEK 4.21B for the closed production-and-storage call (utlysningar page, updated 2026-09-02), 400+ applications worth ~SEK 13B received (Aug-2026). Track 2 "Effektiv energianvändning": dedicated regulation on state aid for more efficient energy use in companies now decided by the government (regeringen.se press release, Sept-2026); support for environmental studies and investment measures raising corporate energy efficiency; first call planned autumn 2026 (agency page updated 2026-09-02: "Utlysningen är ännu inte öppen"). Arctic relevance: northern Sweden (Norrbotten/Västerbotten) gigawatt-scale industrial expansion (green steel, batteries, data centres) is the primary driver of new electricity demand the programme addresses; promoted to regional businesses by North Sweden Cleantech platform. Regulation SFS 2025:1487 in force 2026-01-13; total Kraftlyftet investment-support frame SEK 5B; support intensity max 30% of investment cost for energy-storage projects and up to 45% for other measure types, cap EUR 30M per project; projects must not be started before application, require cost-benefit analysis, and be completed by 2031-12-31; geographic priority elområde 3-4 (southern Sweden) plus local high-need projects in other areas.
properties.eligibility: Companies/projects in Sweden; Track 2 threshold: companies with average annual energy use >2.78 GWh over last 3 years (size-agnostic); measures must be implemented by the energy-using company; apply via Energimyndigheten e-service "Kraftlyftet"
properties.operator: Energimyndigheten (Swedish Energy Agency) under government regulations on state aid for electricity-delivery security and energy efficiency
properties.status: ACTIVE (Track 1 call closed 01-Jul-2026, ~400 applications/SEK 13B under examination Aug-2026, first grant decisions expected late autumn 2026 (senhoesten) per agency via energi.se 04-Aug-2026; application mix ~60% storage of power/heat, ~500 MW new generation in SE3/SE4, 73 bio-power applications (bioenergitidningen 26-Aug-2026); Track 2 förordning on state aid for more efficient energy use in companies enters into force 01-Oct-2026 per regeringen.se, first utlysning planned autumn 2026 — not yet open as of 04-Sep)
properties.sources: energimyndigheten.se news "Stod for produktion och lagring inom Kraftlyftet oppnar 26 februari" (OFFICIAL-GOV, call 26-Feb-07-May-2026, regulation Dec-2025, measure examples) + energimyndigheten.se Kraftlyftet produktion-och-lagring page (OFFICIAL-GOV, closed 01-Jul-2026, applications under review) + energimyndigheten.se kraftlyftet-stod-for-effektiv-energianvandning page (OFFICIAL-GOV, updated 2026-09-02: 2.78 GWh threshold, first call autumn 2026) + energi.se Aug-2026 "Ansokningar for 13 miljarder kronor i Kraftlyftet" (400+ apps) + energinyheter.se 02-Sep-2026 + northswedencleantech.se news (regional promotion). properties.name: Kompleksny proekt razvitiya AZRF i TTK (Comprehensive Arctic Zone + Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor development project) — 271 projects consolidating RUB 32T+ investments
properties.type: Federal comprehensive development project (Arctic Strategy 2035 update tool; VEF-2026, 3 Sep 2026)
properties.benefits: Consolidates 271 investment projects worth over RUB 32 trillion (90%+ private capital) into one comprehensive plan for the Arctic Zone (AZRF) + Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor (TTK/TATC); becomes the main implementation tool of the updated Arctic Strategy through 2035 (approved by Presidential Decree of 26 Mar 2026). Targets by 2035: AZRF GRP doubling from RUB 14T to RUB 28T; 55,000+ new jobs; +1.3 GW capacity in energy-deficient Arctic regions (incl. SMRs and floating power units). Planning horizons: 2030 / 2036 / 2042 / 2050. Anchor projects: Baimsky GOK (Chukotka copper), Arctic LNG-2 + Northern Latitudinal Railway + Sevmash + Yakutia gas (TATC), Murmansk LNG & Murmansk metallurgical cluster + Murmansk transport hub modernization, Tomtor rare-earth deposit (Yakutia), Arkhangelsk deep-water port, Vostok Oil pipeline to Bukhta Sever terminal (Taymyr). VEF-2026 OFFICIAL final wrap-up (erdc.ru 05-Sep + vedomosti press_releases 04-Sep): KRDV x AO VIS x Fond Kristall Rosta investment-mechanism agreement for this comprehensive project official investment sum RUB 1T ('Сумма инвестиций составила 1 трлн рублей' per vedomosti Roscongress wrap-up full text; CORRECTION 05-Sep-2026: earlier 'FROM RUB 1.13T' was a misattribution — the same wrap-up attaches 'от 1 трлн 130 млрд' to the Mohe-Nayba MTK bullet, cross-ref ARC-RAIL-009; = trillion-naming PASS 77: first official party+amount designation of the KRDV-channel trillion mechanism, though at exactly 1T not >1T); Rosatom x KRDV agreement on AZRF+TATC cooperation incl. icebreaker-escort corridor formation — official volume RUB 724.3B; Yakutia x KRDV x KRD-RS cooperation agreement for MTK Mokhe-Nyiba (2 Mt/yr by 2030, от RUB 1.13T official, preliminary pre-FS done without federal budget, international investor consortium forming). Instruments: unified preferential regime (ETOR, see ARC-PROG-706), concessions, long-term OFZs for investors, state guarantees, 'Northern Credit' lending programs, expanded RSU (unfulfilled obligation) mechanism. erdc.ru (3-Sep-2026): plans to attract up to RUB 1T into the comprehensive project (state-levered envelope vs 32T consolidated portfolio).
properties.eligibility: Investors in AZRF subjects (Murmansk, Arkhangelsk, Vologda, Kirov regions, Komi, Karelia, Nenets/Yamalo-Nenets/Khanty-Mansi AO, Yakutia, Chukotka) + TTK corridor projects; resident status via ETOR/AZRF/MTOR regimes; project inclusion in the comprehensive plan (submission to Government by end of 2026)
properties.operator: Minvostokrazvitiya (Dept. of Arctic Development, dir. O. Vakhchin) / Government of the Russian Federation / Rosatom (TATC)

properties.name: Energiberedskapsklivet — Swedish Energy Agency corporate energy-preparedness investment support (civil defence)
properties.city: Eskilstuna (Swedish Energy Agency HQ; nationwide calls)
properties.type: State investment support (investeringsstöd) under Förordning (2026:235) om statligt stöd för energiberedskapsåtgärder
properties.benefits: Grants to companies for physical investments that strengthen energy preparedness, robustness and resilience so operations can maintain energy supply during peacetime crises and heightened military alert (höjd beredskap). Energiberedskapsklivet 2026 can grant approx SEK 790M total, of which at least SEK 60M earmarked for heat/cool measures and at least SEK 60M for gas measures; budget spread over multiple years. Parallel 2026 calls (all close 30-Sep-2026, projects may start earliest 01-Dec-2026): (1) Reservkraft gasförsörjning — backup power for critical electricity to biogas production and gas transmission/distribution; (2) Försörjningsberedskap för gasnät — gas-injection points, spare-parts stock, mobile metering/regulation stations; (3) Skydd av pumpstationer inom värme/kyla och renovering av befintliga värmepannor — physical protection of district heating/cooling pump stations, renovation of existing boilers as standby heat-plant reserves; (4) Mobila värmepannor — mobile heat boilers ensuring continued heat delivery during disruption of ordinary production (separate call; official count is FOUR utlysningar per energimyndigheten.se news 2026-09-04, not three). For 2026 only support for physical investments applies. Arctic relevance: district-heating resilience is critical infrastructure in northern Sweden's long-winter municipalities (Kiruna, Skellefteå, Luleå, Umeå) — actively promoted by Skellefteå kommun näringslivskontor; supports societal security for the region's green-steel/battery/data-centre buildout.
properties.eligibility: Companies (any economic activity, incl. municipal energy companies); this round targets gas network operators, gas producers and district heating/cooling operators; measures must not be legally mandatory duties; apply via Energimyndigheten e-service Mina sidor (company e-authorisation required); cost reallocation between budget lines >10% / >SEK 50k needs agency approval.
properties.operator: Energimyndigheten (Swedish Energy Agency) under government regulation SFS 2026:235
properties.status: ACTIVE (2026 calls open to 30-Sep-2026; ~SEK 790M grantable; knowledge-support + future calls ongoing)
properties.sources: energimyndigheten.se Energiberedskapsklivet main page (OFFICIAL-GOV: SEK 790M 2026 frame, >=60M heat/cool + >=60M gas, measure list, förordning 2026:235 link) + energimyndigheten.se utlysningar pages Reservkraft gasförsörjning / Försörjningsberedskap för gasnät / Skydd av pumpstationer (OFFICIAL-GOV: deadline 2026-09-30, projects start earliest 2026-12-01, target groups) + energimyndigheten.se FAQ page (OFFICIAL-GOV, updated 2026-09-02: physical investments only in 2026) + riksdagen.se Förordning (2026:235) (OFFICIAL legal text) + energinyheter.se 21-May-2026 'Energimyndigheten inför stöd för att stärka företags energiberedskap' (independent trade media) + Skellefteå kommun näringslivskontor post (municipal institutional, northern promotion) + energimyndigheten.se nyhetsarkiv 2026-09-04 'Fyra nya utlysningar för starkt energiberedskap' (OFFICIAL-GOV: four calls confirmed — 2 kraft/fjärrvärme incl. mobila värmepannor + 2 gas; webinar 07-Sep 10:00-10:30 + 18-Sep 14:30-15:00 via Trippus (times verified on Reservkraft gasforsorjning utlysning page, LIVE-CHECK 05-Sep; no live Q&A, questions to finansiering.energiberedskapsklivet@energimyndigheten.se); all open to 30-Sep-2026). properties.name: Yamal (Sabetta) Arctic Integrated Emergency Rescue Center — MChS (opened May 2026)
properties.type: National emergency search & rescue hub (MChS/FMBA/Marine Rescue Service)
properties.benefits: Co-ordinated round-the-clock response to incidents in hard-to-reach Arctic areas incl. NSR; telemedicine, psychological support, radiation/chemical/biological safety; rapid deployment in extreme cold; joint MChS-FMBA duties for Arctic workers and crews.
properties.eligibility: Federal/regional rescue & medical infrastructure serving the Arctic Zone & NSR; joint MChS/FMBA/Marine Rescue Service crews
properties.operator: MChS (Ministry of Emergency Situations) + FMBA + Yamalo-Nenets administration
properties.sources: news-pravda.com (Pravda EN: MES Minister Alexander Kurenkov opened center in Yamal w/ FMBA head Veronika Skvortsova & Yamal Governor Dmitry Artyukhov); usa.news-pravda.com world 2026-05-12 (FMBA: joint MChS-FMBA operations, 170+ telemedicine interventions); telegra.ph (MES-FMBA accord, medical unit Murmansk Pirogov Center). NAME DISAMBIG: this is the Sabetta/Yamal region rescue center, distinct from Novatek Arctic LNG 1 Sabetta cargo terminal (ARC-FAC-315) and Sabetta port zones (ARC-BIZ-004/006).

properties.name: Pevek Arctic Integrated Emergency Rescue Center (first NSR rescue center, est. 2024)
properties.type: National emergency search & rescue hub (MChS)
properties.benefits: First Arctic integrated emergency rescue center of the Russian MChS along the NSR (2024); strengthens round-the-clock rescue readiness in the eastern Arctic; hub for vessel support & coastal incident response.
properties.eligibility: Federal rescue infrastructure serving the eastern NSR & Chukotka; joint MChS/FMBA duties
properties.operator: MChS (Ministry of Emergency Situations) + FMBA
properties.status: ACTIVE (established 2024; joint MChS-FMBA duty in Chukotka)
properties.sources: bellona.org (Monthly Highlights Russian Arctic May 2026 — first MChS integrated emergency rescue center on the NSR established in Pevek 2024; Dikson/Tiksi next); news-mail.ru/society/71798187 (MChS plan: centers opened in Pevek and Sabetta, Tiksi & Dikson next). NAME DISAMBIG: distinct from Pevek Commercial Port (ARC-PORT-005), Pevek Cape Nagleynyn terminal (ARC-PORT-099) and Pevek city (ARC-CITY-006); this is the rescue center.

properties.name: Tiksi Arctic Emergency Services Complex (MChS/FMBA/Rosmorpeflot, 4.07B RUB turnkey)
properties.type: National emergency & safety hub (turnkey, eastern NSR)
properties.benefits: Tiksi becomes the eastern-Russian-Arctic security hub: turnkey complex with administrative-residential buildings, 19-bay garage, medical center & full aviation infrastructure (heated/unheated Mi-38 helicopter hangars, taxiways, 2 helipads); 4.07B RUB tender from MChS Capital Construction Directorate; supports NSR emergency/medical response.
properties.eligibility: Federal MChS/FMBA/Rosmorpeflot facilities; eastern NSR operations hub
properties.operator: Federal State Institution 'Management of Capital Construction for MChS of Russia'; MChS/FMBA/Rosmorpeflot
properties.sources: ulus-media / Uluus Media (4.07B RUB turnkey tender, MChS/FMBA/Rosmorpeflot, 19-bay garage, medical center, Mi-38 hangars/taxiways/2 helipads, est. 2026-2028); bellona.org (Tiksi construction to begin 2026); news-mail.ru (Tiksi slated as next after Pevek/Sabetta). NAME DISAMBIG: distinct from Tiksi Sea Port (ARC-PORT-006), Tiksi East Port (ARC-PORT-036) and Tiksi city (ARC-CITY-007); this is the emergency-services complex.

properties.name: Dikson Arctic Aviation Rescue Center (MChS, planned 2028-2031)
properties.type: Arctic aviation search & rescue center (MChS/FMBA/Marine Rescue Service)
properties.benefits: New Arctic aviation search-and-rescue center on the Arctic coast; joint crews from MChS, FMBA & Marine Rescue Service; protects residents & crews in the northernmost areas; currently served only by a local fire-rescue detachment + regional maritime rescue.
properties.eligibility: Federal/regional rescue infrastructure serving the Taymyr/central NSR; joint MChS/FMBA/Marine Rescue Service crews
properties.operator: MChS (Ministry of Emergency Situations) + FMBA + Marine Rescue Service
properties.sources: news-mail.ru (MChS-announced plan: Arctic aviation search-and-rescue center in Dikson, 2028-2031, joint MChS/FMBA/Marine Rescue Service crews); arhnet.info/news/news-651935 (Archnet/Arkhangelsk: Dikson Arctic aviation-rescue center, Ministry of Emergency Situations). NAME DISAMBIG: Dikson Sea Port (ARC-PORT-007) and Dikson city (ARC-CITY-008) are separate; this is the rescue/aviation center.

properties.name: Murmansk FMBA Arctic Medical-Biological Support Center (NSR flagship, since 2024)
properties.type: Arctic medical & biological support center (FMBA, NSR flagship)
properties.benefits: Flagship medical and biological support center for the NSR since 2024 (FMBA Advanced Medical Unit at the N.I. Pirogov Center): round-the-clock telemedicine, psychological support, radiation/chemical/biological safety; joint MChS-FMBA operations; 170+ emergency telemedicine interventions.
properties.eligibility: Federal FMBA medical/biologic infrastructure for NSR & Arctic workforce; joint MChS-FMBA operations
properties.operator: FMBA (Federal Medical-Biological Agency) + MChS + Murmansk regional authorities
properties.sources: usa.news-pravda.com (Pravda USA 2026-05-12: FMBA flagship medical & biological support center for NSR in Murmansk since 2024, 170+ telemedicine interventions); telegra.ph (FMBA-MES accord, Advanced Medical Unit at Murmansk N.I. Pirogov Center, Yamal ops since Mar 2026). NAME DISAMBIG: distinct from Novatek Murmansk LNG Terminal Belokamenka (ARC-FAC-328); this is the FMBA medical-biologic center.
